statement: The function returns a result r, and r = true iff all three conditions hold: (1) there is a finite path v0,...,vk from source to destination (k >= 0, v0 = source, vk = destination, and for each 0 <= i < k the pair [vi,vi+1] occurs in edges); (2) every finite path v0,...,vk with v0 = source whose last vertex vk is terminal (there is no w with 0 <= w < n such that [vk,w] occurs in edges) has vk = destination; (3) there is no infinite path starting at source, equivalently no directed cycle, including a one-vertex self-loop, is reachable from source by a finite path.
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, overflow, or go out of bounds).
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: If there is no w with 0 <= w < n such that [source,w] occurs in edges, then the function returns a result r and r = true iff source = destination.
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: If there exist k >= 0 and vertices v0,...,vk such that v0 = source, the pair [vi,vi+1] occurs in edges for every 0 <= i < k, vk has no outgoing edge (no w with [vk,w] in edges), and vk != destination, then the function returns a result r and r = false.
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: If there is a directed cycle (including a self-loop v->v) that is reachable from source by a finite path, then the function returns a result r and r = false.
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r = true, there exist k >= 0 and vertices v0,...,vk such that v0 = source, vk = destination, and for every 0 <= i < k the pair [vi,vi+1] occurs in edges. (The case k = 0 is allowed when source = destination.)
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r = true, for every vertex v, if v is reachable from source by a finite path and v has no outgoing edge in edges, then v = destination.
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r = true, no directed cycle, including a self-loop, is reachable from source by a finite path.
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r = true, for every vertex v, if v is reachable from source by a finite path, then there exists a finite path from v to destination.
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r = true, destination has no outgoing edge: there is no w with 0 <= w < n such that [destination,w] occurs in edges.
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: For every two edge lists edges1 and edges2 satisfying the preconditions, if for every u,v with 0 <= u < n and 0 <= v < n the pair [u,v] occurs as an element of edges1 exactly when it occurs as an element of edges2, then the function returns the same Boolean result for (n,edges1,source,destination) and for (n,edges2,source,destination).
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; n <= 10000; both edges1 and edges2 satisfy: every element e has len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; len(edges1) <= 10000 and len(edges2) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and empty edge lists are allowed.

statement: The function returns the same Boolean result when called on (n',edges,source,destination) as when called on (n,edges,source,destination).
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; n <= 10000; n' is an integer with n <= n' <= 10000; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if r = false, then at least one of the following holds: (i) there is a directed cycle, including a self-loop, reachable from source by a finite path; (ii) there exist k >= 0 and vertices v0,...,vk such that v0 = source, each consecutive pair [vi,vi+1] occurs in edges for 0 <= i < k, vk has no outgoing edge, and vk != destination.
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r = true, the set of all finite paths from source to destination is finite. Here a finite path is identified by its vertex sequence v0,...,vk with k >= 0, v0 = source, vk = destination, and each consecutive pair [vi,vi+1] occurring in edges; paths of different lengths or different vertex sequences count as different.
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r = true, every finite path v0,...,vk with v0 = source and each consecutive pair [vi,vi+1] occurring in edges has length k <= n - 1.
preconditions: n >= 1; 0 <= source < n; 0 <= destination < n; every element e of edges satisfies len(e) = 2, 0 <= e[0] < n, and 0 <= e[1] < n; n <= 10000; len(edges) <= 10000. Parallel edges, self-loops, and the empty edge list are allowed.
